learningObjectives: Differentiate UI design from UX design and explain how they work together.
Identify the core stages of a human-centered design process.
Recognize usability, accessibility, and user needs as key design considerations.

activities.title: UI vs UX Explorer
activities.instruction: Match each task to UI or UX.

content.concept: UI focuses on visual interfaces, while UX focuses on the overall user experience and problem-solving.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: User Experience (UX): Optimizing user journeys & problem-solving
User Interface (UI): Designing visual layouts, colors, and typography

activities.title: Human-Centered Design Map
activities.instruction: Explore each stage of the design process.

content.concept: Human-centered design begins by understanding users and iterates through research, definition, ideation, prototyping, and testing.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Good vs Poor Experience
activities.instruction: Select the design with better usability.

content.concept: Usability depends on how easily users can understand, navigate, and complete tasks within an interface.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Clear buttons, readable text, simple navigation
Cluttered layout, hidden menus, tiny fonts

activities.title: UX Design Principles
activities.instruction: Match each principle with its example.

content.concept: Consistency, feedback, visibility, simplicity, and user control help create predictable and usable interfaces.
